citywide.criterion: rises_with_rain: each populated bin's share is at or above the previous bin's Wilson 95% lower bound and the top bin's share exceeds the bottom bin's; strictly_monotone records the no-dips-at-all result
citywide.note: max 2-day rain over all 68 cells of the rain file (the ocean-filtered land + lagoon-shore set); share = days that are catalog flood days (any type)

caveats: unreported is not dry: the catalog is news coverage, not a gauge, so a storm with no report is counted as not flooded even if it flooded
IMERG cells are ~10 km and smooth storm cores: the cell total can miss or dilute the rain that actually fell at a site
thin years: catalog flood days per year are in years[]; years with fewer than 5 are thin and are excluded from the well_searched rates
a strong match means the news named the place or a point near it, not a measured depth
flooded counts only strong (name/near) pluvial matches inside the April-November searched window; riverine, lagoon and coastal days are listed per site in excluded_matches but stay out of the rates
meta.method: Rain-matched storm replay (LAGOS_PLAN roadmap steps 6-7). For each site the IMERG 0.1 deg cell containing its geometry centroid is the site cell (3x3 neighbourhood max kept as sensitivity). A day's rain is the 2-day total (day before + day), the same measure as local_max_2d_mm in flood_days.json, plus the max 30-min rate over the two days. Only days in the April-November months of the years/months actually searched (flood_days meta.search_coverage) enter the rates; Dec-Mar was searched once a year only. A storm is a wet spell of consecutive days with 2-day rain >= 20 mm (or the threshold if lower); a threshold selects spells by their peak, which is the storm's rain; it flooded the site if a strong (name/near) pluvial match falls on any of its days or the day after the last one. Rates carry a Wilson 95% interval. Replay analogs are the storms whose peak is at least the reference storm's 2-day rain at the site cell, minus the reference itself. Before/after splits storms >= 40 mm at the earliest of the promise date, the first claimed_done update and the first claimed_ongoing update, and calls a difference only with at least 5 storms on each side. Missing rain days would be excluded and counted, never treated as zero.
